lens: Applied agricultural-engineering reviewer for Computers and Electronics in Agriculture / Biosystems Engineering. I focused on practical value, field validation, how realistic the data and execution model are, agronomic metrics (skip/overlap in m2/ha, inputs, time), and how the work compares with the agricultural coverage-path-planning (CPP) literature and with commercial auto-guidance practice. Sources I checked directly: docs/research_proposal.md, docs/experiments_report.md, results/tables.md, all figures/*.png, experiments/core.py, exp_lib.py, exp_main.py, exp_real.py, data_citrus.py, data_rtk.py, exp_cross2.py, the results CSVs (main_*_v3, ablation_hard, real), and the literature list.
verdict: REJECT in its current form (resubmission encouraged), not major revision. The user's critique is correct and actually understates the problem. (1) All 15+ baselines are rules for picking one scalar margin lambda on the authors' own greedy planner. For a scalar decision, scenario-with-discarding, CVaR, Cantelli, Gaussian and CE-U are all just different order statistics or moments of the same run-level score. Their ranking therefore mostly reflects which type of guarantee each targets. Scenario (beta=0.01) is a PAC guarantee; CE-U is a marginal guarantee, and its PAC version is the same order statistic. So "6.6% vs 7.9% overlap" is largely a definitional gap, not an algorithmic win. No published agricultural CPP algorithm is compared: not Fields2Cover, Hameed 2016 3D side-to-side, Jin & Tang 3D, or Oksanen-Visala. No genuinely different uncertainty model is compared either: no GP chance constraint, extreme-value theory (EVT), tube-MPC invariant set, or conformal predictive programming over a vector of pass spacings. (2) The execution model behind every main result has a physics problem in core.simulate. The earth-fixed RTK error is injected in the vehicle frame, so its sign flips on alternate passes. All passes are also integrated simultaneously from t=0 with a shared RTK time index. And the only error source is one 27-minute, near-white car RTK series. The calibrated margin of about 9 cm is set by the tail of that single series, so the headline numbers may be artefacts. (3) The terrain story does not hold up agronomically. Paddy fields are levelled terraces. The 30 m Copernicus DSM gradients over 0.3-2.8 ha fields (2-5 cells across) mostly reflect terrace steps, vegetation and DEM noise. That explains the CE-A null result, and it undermines the "hilly vs plain" contrast. (4) There is no real coverage-operation validation. CitrusFarm is an orchard-alley traversal, apparently manually driven (sd 33-43 cm), with non-adjacent rows paired as "adjacent passes" and 10 m strips counted as "operations". It reports overlaps of 34-85%, and CE-U fails 3 of 10 out-of-distribution splits there. (5) The agronomic value case runs the wrong way. Against farmer practice (fixed 10 cm overlap: 3.85% overlap, 1.25 m2/ha missed), CE-U spends about 280 m2/ha of extra double-treated area to avoid about 0.75 m2/ha of miss, which contradicts the input-saving motivation in the introduction. (6) The figures collapse into two clusters (P=0 and P near 0.9). CE-U, CE-A and CE-pair sit on top of each other, field counts differ between figures, tables and CSVs, and one panel is empty. A CEA/BE editor would read this as a simulation study with a thin real-data appendix. A Q1 path does exist: fix the physics, add algorithm-level comparisons with full-field agronomic metrics, run the tests on real slopes, and above all run one genuine autosteer field trial. With those P0 items done this becomes a credible CEA submission. Without a real coverage-operation trial, the realistic ceiling is a lower-tier journal or a methods venue where the theory is judged on its own (and there, Theorem 1 is close to textbook split conformal, so the score design and the decision-dependence results have to carry the novelty).

major_issues.issue: The comparison is between categories of margin rules, not algorithms. Every baseline (nominal, fixed 5/10/30 cm, slope rule, Gaussian/empirical/conformal pointwise, Gaussian score, Cantelli, scenario, CVaR, Wasserstein DRO-CVaR, worst-case, GBM-QR, CQR) only chooses lambda in h_k = w/2 - lambda*sigma_k on the authors' greedy planner (exp_lib.py, exp_main.py). The comparisons also mix guarantee types. Scenario with discarding at beta=0.01 (exp_lib.scenario_lambda) is exactly a training-conditional (PAC) conformal quantile. CVaR and DRO control a different risk measure. CE-U controls marginal probability. 'CE-U has the lowest overlap among valid methods' is therefore mostly because CE-U targets the weakest guarantee.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: A CEA/BE reviewer from the CPP community will ask how CE compares with Fields2Cover, Hameed et al. 2016 (which explicitly minimises skip/overlap between swaths on 3D terrain), Jin & Tang 2011 and Oksanen & Visala 2009, and none are there. A statistics or controls reviewer will note that for a 1-D decision all these baselines are quantile estimators of the same score, so the 'win' over scenario is the price of PAC confidence, not a better algorithm. Either reading gives an 'insufficient comparison' rejection.
major_issues.concrete_fix:
Add a three-tier comparison and make it Section 5.1.
(a) Planner-level published algorithms, each with its published defaults plus industry overlap, and each again with CE as a plug-in layer:
- Fields2Cover (pip install fields2cover==2.1.0, confirmed on PyPI from this sandbox): constant-width headland, BruteForce swath-angle optimisation (NSwath / SwathLength objectives), Boustrophedon/Snake route, Dubins/Reeds-Shepp turns.
- Hameed 2016 side-to-side 3D spacing correction (deterministic per-pass spacing from projected width w*cos(side slope)).
- Jin & Tang 2011 terrain-aware swath direction.
- Oksanen-Visala trapezoidal decomposition, using F2C decomposition on non-convex polygons.
Metrics: full-field overlap including headlands, missed m2/ha, number of swaths, total path length, turn count, operating time.
(b) Statistical/uncertainty algorithms with genuinely different models: GP chance constraint (Hewing 2020), GEV/EVT on run maxima, Rice-formula excursion, moving-block bootstrap, tube-MPC minimal robust positively invariant (mRPI) bound, and conformal predictive programming over the vector of pass spacings (a vector decision, solved as a MILP with scipy.optimize.milp or OR-tools).
(c) Guarantee-matched comparisons: CE-PAC(delta=0.01) next to Scenario(beta=0.01). They should coincide; say so honestly. Sweep every method's own tuning parameter (eps, overlap cm, CVaR level, DRO radius, GP quantile) and report overlap at matched realised violation (interpolated on the frontier) as the headline number.
major_issues.effort: 5-8 days coding and compute; fully feasible here (fields2cover, scikit-learn GP, scipy genextreme/pyextremes, OR-tools are all on PyPI).

major_issues.issue:
Execution-model physics bug and an under-sampled GNSS error model (core.simulate, data_rtk.py).
(i) `meas = d + ... + rtk_scale*rtk[ti]` adds the RTK error in the vehicle frame, and `rec = sgn*d` maps it back. The field-frame error is therefore -sgn*rtk, flipping on every alternate pass, although GNSS error is earth-fixed. A largely common-mode error becomes maximally anti-correlated between adjacent passes (about 2x rtk in e_{k+1}-e_k).
(ii) All K passes are integrated in parallel from t=0 with one time index `ti = offset + int(t*dt)`. The real 60-150 s separation between adjacent passes (pass duration plus headland turn), which is where RTK drift creates pass-to-pass error, is absent.
(iii) The only GNSS source is one 1615-epoch (27 min) car series: lag-1 autocorrelation 0.33 (essentially white at 1 Hz, which is untypical of RTK; check time-alignment artefacts), one 19 cm outlier. It is recycled for every run and zero-order-held, so the controller sees 1 Hz steps.
(iv) The slip gain (-k_s*0.35*g_lat), OU roughness and roll-compensation c~0.85 are not identified on any data.
(v) No implement model (trailed-implement drift on slopes) and no geometric slope projection.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: The certified margin of about 9 cm is the (1-eps) quantile of a field-wide supremum, so it is driven by the extreme tail of this one series and by the sign-flip artefact. A reviewer who reads the code, or simply asks 'how is GNSS error applied across passes', will conclude the main results may be artefacts of the simulator. The claim of 'real RTK error injected' is also misleading when the error is projected in a car's body frame and re-applied in a tractor body frame.
major_issues.concrete_fix:
1. Inject the 2-D (E,N) GNSS error in the earth frame and project it onto the field's lateral axis.
2. Simulate passes sequentially with real timing (cumulative pass time plus turn time from F2C path length).
3. Replace the single series with many hours of real GNSS error at several service tiers. NOAA CORS RINEX on the public bucket s3://noaa-cors-pds (verified reachable from this sandbox), processed with RTKLIB (rtklibexplorer demo5 from GitHub, or pyrtklib 0.2.7 on PyPI), gives: short-baseline RTK between neighbouring stations, PPP, SBAS/DGNSS-like and single-point solutions on static stations with known coordinates. That yields many independent days with correct low-frequency structure. Check the sampling rate; most daily files are 30 s, so keep the i2Nav series only for the high-frequency component.
4. Add a trailed-implement drift model and the cos(theta) projection.
5. Validate the simulator: report its ISO 12188-2-style pass-to-pass error (15-min interval) and compare it with published autosteer measurements (Gan-Mor et al. 2007; Easterly et al. 2010).
6. Re-run E1-E9 and state in the paper that v3 results were superseded.
major_issues.effort: 3-5 days (RTKLIB processing about 1 day, simulator refactor about 1 day, re-runs 1-3 days of compute); feasible here.

major_issues.issue: Terrain data are misused, which is also why the terrain-adaptive variant (CE-A) shows no gain. The 'hilly paddy' set (mean slope 1.6 deg, max 7.7 deg) comes from 30 m Copernicus GLO-30, which is a DSM, sampled over fields of 0.26-2.8 ha, only 2-5 DEM cells across. Paddies are levelled for ponding, so the DEM gradient reflects terrace risers, vegetation and DEM noise, not the side slope a machine experiences. The North China Plain wheat slopes (about 0.9 deg) are within DEM noise. The simulator nonetheless applies slope-driven slip and antenna-roll offsets inside paddies. CE-A vs CE-U overlap: Wilcoxon p = 0.41 (paddy) and 0.90 (wheat).
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Any Chinese agricultural-engineering reviewer knows terraced paddies are level within each paddy. The physical mechanism claimed for paddy errors is wrong, the 'hilly vs plain' natural experiment is not one, and the terrain-adaptive contribution has no evidence. Paddy errors come from hardpan unevenness, sinkage and wheel slip in mud, and that is not modelled.
major_issues.concrete_fix:
(a) For paddy, either treat the fields as level and model paddy-specific error sources (hardpan depth variation, sinkage-induced slip, citing paddy autosteer studies in Trans. CSAE), or drop the slope mechanism there.
(b) Add a genuinely sloped dataset: USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar DEM (public s3://prd-tnm, verified reachable) over sloping cropland, e.g. the Palouse (WA/ID) with 5-20% side slopes or the Iowa loess hills. Digitise polygons from imagery or use fiboa/Fields-of-The-World boundaries if reachable.
(c) Add the geometric projection effect (horizontal coverage w*cos(theta); about 1% of width at 8 deg, 2.7 cm on a 3 m implement, which is the same order as the margins) and trailed-implement drift.
(d) Run a controlled heterogeneity sweep: plot the CE-A overlap saving against within-field side-slope heterogeneity (std of 1 m slope across passes). If the gain still does not appear, remove CE-A from the contributions.
major_issues.effort: 3-6 days (3DEP tiles, polygons, re-runs); feasible here, except fiboa/source.coop, whose TLS failed from this sandbox (check the proxy README).

major_issues.issue: No real coverage-operation validation. CitrusFarm (exp_real.py, data_citrus.py) is a Jackal in orchard alleys spaced about 6.1-6.4 m apart. Lateral error sd is 33.5/43.1/35.2 cm and p95 is 65-83 cm per block, which is consistent with manual or joystick driving (verify in Teng et al. 2023). The 'planned line' is a lattice fitted afterwards to pass means. Windows of K passes consecutive in time are treated as adjacent swaths, but the row-index sequences are e.g. 0,-5,-10,... and 0,6,1,5,2,..., i.e. physically non-adjacent. 'Operations' are 10 m strips, the implement is a virtual 6 m one, and the resulting overlaps are 34-85%. Out of distribution, CE-U falls to 0.833 (LOBO 13D, K=5) and 0.858 (LODO 07-16, K=3), while scenario and CVaR hold.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: CEA and BE expect a field experiment on a real machine doing a real coverage operation. This replay is not one: it measures human alley-following, not autosteer pass-to-pass error, and pairs non-adjacent rows. Overlaps of 36-82% make any agronomic reading impossible, and the one real-data result that tests exchangeability (LOBO/LODO) is where the method fails.
major_issues.concrete_fix:
(a) Decisive fix, done by the authors' lab: a real autosteer trial.
- Commercial Chinese RTK autosteer (CHCNAV/FJDynamics/Huace-class) on a tractor, rice transplanter or combine.
- 3-6 fields including at least one genuinely sloped upland field; at least 10 repeated operations per field of at least 15 passes.
- A second RTK/PPK rover on the implement as ground truth.
- Realised skips/overlaps checked by UAV orthophoto (seeded rows or a water-sensitive/dye tracer).
- Follow the ISO 12188-2 protocol.
Calibrate on early operations and certify later ones and new fields.
(b) Minimum work inside this sandbox:
- Restrict CitrusFarm windows to physically adjacent rows (sequences 01, 05, 07 and the monotone parts of 03/04).
- Relabel it a 'manual-driving regime stress test' and drop the overlap-% claims.
- Use block-level hierarchical conformal for LOBO/LODO.
- Search GitHub for real autosteer logs (ISOXML TaskData TLG samples in AgGateway ADAPT or isoxml repositories, AgOpenGPS logs; availability unverified).
(c) Treat the harvester GNSS trajectories as real evidence of current practice: measure realised pass spacing and overlap of human-driven harvesters, if their sampling rate and accuracy allow.
major_issues.effort: (a) 2-4 weeks including field days, outside this sandbox; (b) 1-2 days here; (c) 0.5-1 day here.

major_issues.issue:
Neither the agronomic metric nor the value case holds up.
- The certified event is zero missed area at any 1 m cross-section, with no width tolerance: a 1 mm by 1 m sliver counts as failure.
- In main_paddy_v3 (60 fields): nominal misses 47.8 m2/ha (0.48%); fixed 10 cm (farmer practice) has 3.85% overlap and 1.25 m2/ha missed; CE-U has 6.65% overlap and 0.5 m2/ha missed.
- So CE-U adds about 280 m2/ha of double-treated area to avoid about 0.75 m2/ha of miss relative to practice, which contradicts the FAO/pesticide input-saving motivation.
- CE-R (the risk certificate) is practically identical to fixed 5 cm (1.9% overlap, 6.6 vs 6.1 per-10,000 missed).
- Overlap is computed on the main area only (exp_lib.overlap_ratio), excluding headlands, where most real overlap occurs.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: A CEA/BE reviewer judges practical value in kg/ha, CNY/ha and ha/h. Under RTK the method increases input use compared with current practice to remove an agronomically negligible miss. The comparison that favours CE (against scenario and CVaR) is between methods farmers do not use, and the zero-tolerance event has no agronomic meaning: spray patterns overlap, and a 1-2 cm seeding gap is within guess-row tolerance.
major_issues.concrete_fix:
1. Make the score tolerance-aware. A miss is a gap wider than tau_w (operation-specific: combine uncut strip about 5 cm, seeder guess-row tolerance, sprayer boom-edge pattern) persisting longer than tau_l. Lemma 1 extends by replacing lambda(sigma_k+sigma_{k+1}) with lambda(sigma_k+sigma_{k+1})+tau_w plus a morphological opening along s.
2. Report missed and overlapped m2/ha (including headlands, via Fields2Cover), maximum gap width, extra swaths, path length, time and fuel.
3. Add an economic decision analysis in CNY/ha with explicit, cited price assumptions (input cost per ha per application, yield value, contract-harvesting fee), including the break-even miss penalty.
4. Build a regime map (heatmap): CE saving vs practice across GNSS tier (RTK/PPP/SBAS/sub-metre Beidou), slope, implement width, controller and manual driving.
5. Reframe the claim: CE gives the minimal certified track spacing for a given GNSS tier and controller, and saves inputs or increases field capacity where practice is either unsafe (sub-metre guidance, steep slopes) or over-conservative (combine header utilisation of about 85-90%, which affects ha/h).
major_issues.effort: 2-3 days (score change, cost model, regime-map sweep); feasible here.

major_issues.issue: Figures collapse and are inconsistent; this is the user's second critique. Fig3 is a dot strip at P=0 plus a cluster at about 0.9, with separate overlap bars and no trade-off view. CE-U and CE-A are indistinguishable, and CE-U and CE-pair are identical in Fig4. Field counts disagree: Fig3 says 19/10 fields, tables.md 27/16, the v3 CSVs 60/37. Labels overlap in Fig3 ('1 infeasible' over the numbers, colliding x labels), Fig6(b) is empty, and Fig6(a) labels overlap (CE-U*/CQR). Fig4(b) shows 36-82% overlaps.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Q1 reviewers read figures first. A main figure where 7 of 17 methods sit at 0 and the rest overlap near 0.9 carries almost no information, mismatched counts suggest results are being cherry-picked or are still running, and the empty panel and colliding labels signal an unfinished manuscript.
major_issues.concrete_fix:
1. Freeze the experiment version and regenerate every figure and table from one script with the same field set.
2. Redesign Fig3 as a cost-reliability frontier: x = full-field overlap (% or m2/ha), y = realised violation rate (1-P) on a log axis. Each method is a curve swept over its own parameter, with its default setting marked, the target band shaded, and the overlap at matched violation annotated.
3. Put the failing practice baselines on a log axis of missed m2/ha, where they separate (47.8, 6, 1.25 ...) instead of all sitting at P=0.
4. Add per-field paired differences (overlap minus CE-U, valid methods only) and a CNY/ha bar.
5. Merge CE-A into CE-U in the main figure and show CE-A only in the heterogeneity-sweep figure, where it differs.

major_issues.issue:
Too many claimed contributions have null or negative evidence:
- CE-A ~ CE-U (p 0.41/0.90).
- CE-pair equals CE-U on real data and costs about 4.6 percentage points more overlap in simulation (11.4% vs 6.6% paddy).
- Fixed-point calibration matches naive calibration in both default and hard regimes (hard: 27.2% vs 28.0% overlap, P 0.921 vs 0.918).
- Weighted CP gives no benefit under the shifts tried.
- CE-R is about 4.5x conservative because B=1 with n=500 makes B/(n+1) of the same order as alpha=0.003.
- Tube-MPC coupling is claimed but not implemented.
- Generality (mowing/UAV) is claimed but not shown.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Listing seven 'innovations' of which four show no effect reads as inflation. Reviewers will discount the whole contribution list and question why non-functional variants are in the paper.
major_issues.concrete_fix:
1. Cut the contributions to what the data support: (1) the pass-to-pass supremum score, backed by the existing ablation (the pointwise score fails at P=0; the absolute-error score costs +55-65% overlap); (2) the certificate plus the regime map; (3) cross-field deployment with no history on the new field.
2. Move CE-A, weighted CP and the fixed-point step into a 'when it matters' section with constructed heterogeneity and decision-dependence where their effect is demonstrated.
3. Add a location-scale variant that subtracts a learned direction-dependent bias. The alternating-direction slope offset makes adjacent pairs systematically converge or diverge, so shifting pass centres non-uniformly is where terrain information should pay.
4. Tighten CE-R: derive a physical B from assumption A1 and the controller tube, or use Learn-then-Test, and sweep alpha and n.
5. Remove tube-MPC and generality claims unless implemented.

major_issues.issue: Calibration data provenance and deployment realism. In-field calibration uses n_cal=100 past operations on the same field, while a farm runs about 2-8 operations per field per year. Routine autosteer logs record GNSS-measured cross-track error, not the true implement position, so the calibration score is not observable from normal machine data. The cross-field setting is realistic but secondary, and with exchangeable simulated fields its validity holds by construction (the theorem guarantees it). The only real test of exchangeability (LOBO/LODO) fails 3 of 10 times.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Practitioners and reviewers will ask where the 100 ground-truthed operations come from. Showing validity on data the simulator makes exchangeable is circular, and the paper needs evidence that the certificate survives real heterogeneity across fields, days and operators.
major_issues.concrete_fix:
1. Make cross-field (one operation per field, 20-200 fields) the main experiment and in-field calibration with n of 20 or fewer the secondary one.
2. Specify the measurement protocol (implement-mounted RTK/PPK rover, or UAV-measured row spacing) and run an errors-in-variables sensitivity: add measurement noise to the calibration scores and report how validity degrades.
3. Use hierarchical/two-layer conformal (one score per field or block, Dunn et al. 2023; Lee, Barber & Willett 2023) for new-field and new-day certificates, and report LOBO/LODO results with it.

major_issues.issue: Positioning in the literature is missing. The repository's 100-paper list (literature/path_planning_control_100.md) contains no agricultural CPP and no auto-guidance-accuracy paper. Introduction statistics rely on a blog tag page (agronomy.emu.ee/tag/gps) and a market report, and no ISO guidance-test standard is cited.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: CEA/BE reviewers often come from this very literature (Bochtis, Oksanen, Hameed, de Bruin, Tang, Adamchuk groups). Omitting it signals that the authors don't know the field, and blog-sourced headline numbers are unacceptable.
major_issues.concrete_fix:
Add and discuss:
- Agricultural CPP: Oksanen & Visala 2009 (JFR); Jin & Tang 2010 (Trans. ASABE) and 2011 (JFR); Hameed 2013 (JIRS) and 2016 (RAS); Bochtis & Vougioukas 2008 (Biosyst. Eng.); Spekken & de Bruin 2013 (Precis. Agric.); Mier et al. 2023 (Fields2Cover, RA-L); Hoffmann et al. 2024 review (JFR).
- Guidance accuracy and testing: ISO 12188-1/-2; Gan-Mor et al. 2007 (CEA, implement lateral accuracy under RTK); Easterly et al. 2010 (CEA, auto-guidance testing).
- Economics: Batte & Ehsani 2006 (CEA); Luck et al. 2010 (CEA, section control); Shockley et al. 2011.
- Chinese paddy autosteer work in Trans. CSAE (e.g. the SCAU Luo Xiwen/Zhang Zhigang group).
- Conformal planning: Lindemann et al. 2023 (RA-L); Dixit et al. 2023 (L4DC); Zhao et al. 2024 (conformal predictive programming).
Replace the blog statistic with peer-reviewed overlap measurements. Verify every bibliographic detail.

major_issues.issue: Field geometry and operation realism. Polygons are convex hulls of DBSCAN clusters of harvester GNSS points, which inflates area and erases concavities; non-convex fields are dropped. Only the main area is evaluated, with headlands and turns ignored. A single 3 m implement is used for all crops, whereas paddy half-feed combines are about 1.5-2.2 m and transplanters 1.8-2.4 m. No operation type (harvest, seeding, spraying) is specified, so tolerances and costs are undefined.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Applied reviewers check whether the scenario matches a real machine and operation. Generic 3 m implements on convex hulls of 0.3-2.8 ha fields with headlands excluded do not, and they bias overlap downward.
major_issues.concrete_fix:
1. Use alpha-shape polygons checked against imagery and report the polygon error.
2. Run Fields2Cover headlands, decomposition and turns.
3. Choose 1-2 primary operations (e.g. combine harvesting of wheat and rice transplanting or seeding) with matching machine widths, speeds and tolerances.
4. Report full-field metrics.

major_issues.issue:
Reporting and statistics:
- Inconsistent field counts (see the figures issue).
- The E3b wheat run has 1-2 repeats with NaN confidence intervals.
- 'Fields not significantly below target: 89%' is shown without the theoretical reference that conditional coverage given the calibration set follows Beta(n+1-l, l).
- Holm p-values sit at the floor value (2.4e-07) for every comparison, so they carry no effect-size information.
- No variance across calibration draws in the main experiment.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Statistical reviewers will ask whether the per-field shortfalls are expected or a violation, and why p-values replace effect sizes. Incomplete repeats look like work in progress.
major_issues.concrete_fix:
1. Overlay the theoretical Beta distribution of per-field conditional coverage on the empirical histogram.
2. Report overlap differences in percentage points and m2/ha with bootstrap confidence intervals over fields.
3. Complete at least 10 repeats for every cross-field setting.
4. Report variability across calibration draws.

major_issues.issue: The online drift and ACI evidence is weak. In simulation the drift is a synthetic linear soil-moisture ramp. On real data, ACI covers only 49 (K=3) and 24 (K=5) strips, and the static method has zero misses at K=3 (fewer than ACI), so the figure does not demonstrate a need for adaptation.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: The online claim rests on a synthetic ramp and a real stream too short to show anything.
major_issues.concrete_fix:
1. Use multi-day real GNSS error series (NOAA CORS via RTKLIB) and seasonal condition changes taken from the field trial.
2. Compare ACI with DtACI (Gibbs & Candes 2024) and conformal PID (Angelopoulos et al. 2023), and with scenario or fixed baselines.
3. Report long-run miss frequency, overlap cost and the q_t trajectory.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Fields2Cover (full agricultural CPP pipeline)
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Mier G., Valente J., de Bruin S., Fields2Cover: an open-source coverage path planning library for unmanned agricultural vehicles, IEEE RA-L, 2023 (volume/pages to verify)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: pip install fields2cover==2.1.0 (confirmed on PyPI). For each real polygon: constant-width headland of 2-3 w; BruteForce swath angle with NSwath and SwathLength objectives; Boustrophedon and Snake route; Dubins/Reeds-Shepp turns with r_min of 4-6 m. Baselines: F2C at nominal width, F2C with track spacing = w minus the industry overlap, and F2C with effective width w-2q*sigma (CE plug-in), plus re-optimising the angle under CE. Execute the swaths in the fixed simulator and report full-field overlap including headlands, missed m2/ha, path length, turns and time.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Side-to-side 3D CPP to minimise skip/overlap between swaths
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Hameed I.A., la Cour-Harbo A., Osen O.L., Robotics and Autonomous Systems 76 (2016) 36-45 (verify)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: From the 1 m 3DEP DEM, compute each pass's side slope and set the deterministic spacing so that projected widths w*cos(theta) abut (plus their overlap setting). Compare Hameed alone, Hameed plus fixed overlap, and Hameed plus CE on the residual score. This is the most direct published competitor to CE-A.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: 3D-terrain coverage path planning (terrain-aware swath direction)
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Jin J., Tang L., J. Field Robotics 28(3), 2011; and Jin & Tang, Trans. ASABE 53(1), 2010 for 2D (verify)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Choose the swath direction by minimising headland turning cost plus a slope/erosion cost from the DEM (their cost model), then apply the CE margin. Compare against CE-A with direction optimisation; under CE the effective width depends on side slope, so certified coverage and direction optimisation interact.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Field decomposition for non-convex fields
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Oksanen T., Visala A., Coverage path planning algorithms for agricultural field machines, J. Field Robotics 26(8), 2009 (verify)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Use F2C's trapezoidal/boustrophedon decomposition on alpha-shape (non-convex) polygons in place of convex hulls; apply CE per cell; report total swaths and overlap.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Commercial auto-guidance practice emulation
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: ISO 12188-2:2012; manufacturer RTK/PPP/SBAS pass-to-pass specs (Trimble, John Deere, CHCNAV); Gan-Mor et al. 2007 CEA 59 (verify)

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: GP-based chance-constrained margin (cautious planning)
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Hewing L., Kabzan J., Zeilinger M.N., Cautious MPC using Gaussian process regression, IEEE TCST 28(6), 2020 (verify)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Fit sklearn GaussianProcessRegressor to e_{k+1}(s)-e_k(s) on (side slope, direction, s). Set the margin from the predictive quantile with a Bonferroni correction over field cross-sections, or with a Rice-formula correction. This is an uncalibrated Bayesian competitor with a genuinely different model.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Extreme-value theory on run maxima
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Coles S., An Introduction to Statistical Modeling of Extreme Values, Springer 2001
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Fit a GEV (scipy.stats.genextreme or pyextremes 2.5.0 on PyPI) to the calibration run scores S, set lambda to the (1-eps) GEV quantile, and add a PAC variant via profile-likelihood bounds. This is the natural parametric competitor for supremum scores.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Rice-formula excursion probability (Gaussian process supremum)
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Rice S.O., Bell Syst. Tech. J. 1944/45; Adler R.J., Taylor J.E., Random Fields and Geometry, Springer 2007
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Estimate the variance and second spectral moment of the pass-to-pass difference process from calibration runs. Approximate P(sup > u) as N_pairs*L*sqrt(lambda2)/(2*pi*sigma)*exp(-u^2/(2*sigma^2)), solve for u at level eps, and set lambda = u/2.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Tube MPC / minimal robust positively invariant set bound
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Mayne D.Q., Seron M.M., Rakovic S.V., Automatica 41(2), 2005; Rakovic et al., IEEE TAC 2005 (mRPI approximation) (verify)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: For the LQR-I closed loop in core._lqr_gains, compute an outer approximation of the mRPI set under a disturbance bound estimated from calibration data, and use its lateral extent as a robust margin. This replaces the ad hoc 'max score' worst-case baseline and grounds the proposal's tube-MPC claim.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Conformal predictive programming over the vector of pass spacings
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Zhao Y., Yu X., Deshmukh J.V., Lindemann L., arXiv 2402.07407, 2024 (verify)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Make the decision the vector of spacings Delta_k (not one lambda). Minimise sum Delta_k^{-1} (or the number of swaths) subject to a conformal chance constraint on the pass-to-pass score, as a MILP with scipy.optimize.milp or OR-tools (pip). This competitor genuinely differs from CE's one-parameter family.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Training-conditional (PAC) conformal, guarantee-matched to the scenario approach
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Vovk V., Conditional validity of inductive conformal predictors, ACML 2012; Campi M.C., Garatti S., JOTA 148(2), 2011 (verify)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Choose the order statistic l with BinomCDF(n-l; n, eps) <= delta. Report CE-PAC(delta=0.01) next to Scenario(beta=0.01) and state that they coincide for d=1. The headline comparison must be guarantee-matched.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Hierarchical / two-layer conformal for new field, block or day
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Dunn R., Wasserman L., Ramdas A., JASA 2023; Lee Y., Barber R.F., Willett R., Distribution-free inference with hierarchical data, 2023 (verify venue)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Draw one score per field or block (or use the pooled-CDF method) and calibrate at the field level. Apply to the cross-field setting and to the CitrusFarm LOBO/LODO splits where CE-U currently fails.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Online conformal under drift: DtACI and conformal PID
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Gibbs I., Candes E., JMLR 2024; Angelopoulos A., Candes E., Tibshirani R., Conformal PID control, NeurIPS 2023
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Implement both in a few lines alongside the existing ACI and compare on multi-day real GNSS drift and on the field-trial stream: long-run miss frequency, overlap cost, and q_t.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Learn-then-Test for the risk certificate
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Angelopoulos A., Bates S., Candes E., Jordan M., Lei L., Learn then Test, arXiv 2110.01052 (journal version to verify)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Replace CRC with B=1 by LTT with Hoeffding-Bentkus or WSR p-values on the surrogate loss, or derive a physical B from assumption A1. Report the realised-to-target E[miss] ratio, which is about 4.5x now.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Moving-block bootstrap quantile of the score
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Block-bootstrap the per-run scores (or the error series) to estimate the (1-eps) quantile and its confidence. This is a cheap, widely used engineering competitor.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Headland-pattern route optimisation (time/fuel side of the comparison)
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Bochtis D.D., Vougioukas S.G., Biosystems Engineering 101(1), 2008; Spekken M., de Bruin S., Precision Agriculture 14, 2013 (verify)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Use F2C route planners or a small TSP (OR-tools) over swath order to report non-working distance and time for each method's swath set. CE's extra passes then carry their real time and fuel cost.
